Array.prototype.flatMap()

The flatMap() method maps each element and flattens the result by one level in a single traversal, avoiding a separate map() then flat() pass.

callback
Function that produces an element of the new array, taking three arguments: the current element, its index and the array being traversed.
thisArg Optional
Value to use as this when executing callback. Ignored when callback is an arrow function, since arrow functions do not bind their own this.
arr.flatMap(x => [x, x * 2])

The result array is a new array; the original array is left unmodified. Depth is fixed at one level, unlike flat(depth), which accepts an arbitrary depth argument.

Browsercompat-table-never-shown
Node.jsSupported

A naïve implementation loops twice – once to map, once to flatten; flatMap does both in a single pass, and engines can special-case the combined operation for a modest speedup on large arrays.

Related methods worth comparing: map() alone (no flattening), flat() alone (no mapping), and reduce() combined with concat() (the pre-flatMap idiom most codebases used before broad engine support landed).

A common use is expanding each input item into zero, one, or several output items in a single step: return an empty array to drop an item, a one-element array to keep it unchanged, or a multi-element array to expand it, all from the same callback without a separate filter pass.

// drop falsy values, duplicate the rest
[1, 0, 2, null, 3].flatMap(x => x ? [x, x] : [])

Specification: defined in the current ECMAScript language specification under the Array.prototype section; the method reads the array's length once at the start and does not observe elements appended to the array by the callback during iteration, matching the behaviour of map() and forEach().
